headline: High: OpenMetadata can expose metadata to Prefect via APIs/webhooks while Prefect’s broad egress and shared workflow context create leakage, conflict, and cascading-error risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit content through APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP, while Prefect can consume API-driven workflow inputs. A shared channel exists, so attacker-controlled metadata or webhook payloads could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata webhooks or MCP payloads are routed into Prefect task parameters without sanitization
IF Prefect parses catalog or event content as executable instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of webhook text into task prompts
Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from OpenMetadata to Prefect
Insert a manual review step before any task uses catalog-generated text
Log and reject payloads containing instruction-like markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge, while Prefect has broad network egress. If shared metadata or workflow context includes sensitive fields, Prefect can transmit them outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default API-based integrations, but the profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF sensitive catalog metadata is passed from OpenMetadata into Prefect task inputs
IF Prefect tasks send those inputs to external services over network egress
mitigations: Restrict Prefect tasks to redacted metadata only
Turn off outbound calls for workflows handling governance data
Review and classify fields before syncing them between systems
Add a short-lived staging copy with sensitive columns removed
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Prefect egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and API/MCP-based operations, while Prefect is an orchestrator with broad egress but no explicit shared write target or overlapping mutable resource is documented. A write conflict is possible only if an operator points both at the same backend or repo, which is unusual configuration. Uncertainty does not justify medium because no shared writable surface is shown.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external datastore or repository
IF no locking or coordination layer is added around shared writes
mitigations: Assign separate write targets for each agent
Use a lock or lease around shared mutable resources
Schedule writes so only one agent updates a resource at a time
Audit for overlapping credentials before deployment
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can produce lineage, quality, and governance outputs that Prefect may use in orchestration decisions. If Prefect treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad catalog entry can cascade into incorrect workflow actions. The profiles show a plausible producer-consumer chain, but not a verified verification step, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes OpenMetadata outputs without validation
IF workflow decisions are derived directly from catalog or lineage assertions
mitigations: Require a validation step before Prefect acts on catalog data
Compare OpenMetadata outputs against a second source of truth
Flag low-confidence lineage or governance records for review
Limit automation to non-destructive actions until verified
requires-engineering: add schema and semantic checks

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and memory/tribal knowledge, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and has broad egress. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a generic compliance-gap risk is supportable. Because the other agent is not tied to a specific regulated region or regime, it is not appropriate to escalate beyond low.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are stored in OpenMetadata and then exported through Prefect
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Document which data classes may flow between the tools
Align retention settings for shared metadata
Exclude regulated fields from Prefect logs
Review export paths for subject-rights requests
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
